rv.q: My favorite comes near the end, after a mass migration to the other side , when a few lingering souls not ready to cross over wake up and discover that they “had again been granted the great mother-gift: time. More time.” What is opera if not a granting of that gift?

Booker prizewinning novel of the same name may not seem an intuitive choice for adaptation. It’s set over a single night in Georgetown’s Oak Hill Cemetery, where a colourful cast of limbo dwellers battle for the soul of Abraham Lincoln’s deceased 11-year-old son Willie as the president struggles to reclaim his resolve.
It’s a thrilling overture to a mostly disappointing night.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this ambitious Met Opera adaptation of Saunders's novel, with praise for its literary scope and emotional resonance but criticism that the execution disappoints despite thrilling moments.
